source: Hebrew Gospel of Luke v2.1 (Van Rensburg 2026, Vat. Ebr. 100)
method: Consonantal analysis — niqqud stripped, no English/Greek reference provided

verses.translation: And it came to pass that Yeshua was praying in a certain place, when he entered into a certain village [or: tower], and there was there a woman whose name [was] her sister Martha — Martha — and she said to him, Help me, lord! You — [are you not concerned about] the bread [or: food] for them?

translation_notes: ישוע (consonants ישוע): Candidates: H3442 'Jeshua/Yeshua', H3443 same. Chose H3442 as a proper name — the subject who is praying.
במקום (consonants מקום): Candidates: H4725 'a place/standing spot', H6965 'to rise'. With prefix ב- and following אחד, 'in a certain place' is the coherent reading.
אחד: Candidates: H258 'to unify', H259 'one/first'. 'One' modifying 'place' = 'a certain place' is standard Hebrew usage.
בעד: H1157 'after/when/for'. In temporal context of entering, 'when/after' fits the narrative sequence.
במגדל: Candidates: H4026 'tower/village (Migdal)'. This is likely a place name (Migdal/Magdala) or the word for village/tower. The narrative of entering a settlement fits.
שם: Candidates: H8033 'there', H8034 'name'. Both work; 'there' fits with 'and there was there' followed by שמה as 'her name'.
שמה: Candidates: H8047 'ruin', H8048 'Shammah (name)'. However, in context this reads as ש + מה or שם + ה (her name). 'Her name' fits — introducing the woman's identity.
אדון: Candidates: H113 'lord/sovereign', H114 'Addon (name)'. She addresses Yeshua as 'lord/master'.
את/אתה: These together form an emphatic 'you/you yourself'. H859 for the pronoun 'you'.

הלהם / הלהן: These appear to be ה (interrogative/definite) + להם/להן (to them masc/fem). The pair likely represents a scribal doublet or variant — 'to them' addressing both genders, or a correction. In context Martha is asking about serving food to them.
textual_notes: במגדל א׳ — 'tower one' could be a place name (Migdal, i.e., Magdala) with abbreviation mark, or 'a certain tower/village'. The abbreviation mark א׳ suggests a truncated word.
והיתה is repeated twice — possibly a scribal dittography or intentional repetition.
The relationship between שם and שמה is ambiguous: 'there, whose name [was]' or 'there [was] a ruin' or 'there [was] Shammah'. Context of introducing Martha supports 'her name'.

הלהם / הלהן — the pair is unusual. Could be: (1) interrogative ה + ל + הם/הן = 'is it not for them?'; (2) ה + לחם = 'the bread' (with ה+להם being a compressed form); (3) a scribal correction from masculine to feminine pronoun. The parallel with לחם (bread) is suggestive given Martha's role as hostess.
מרתא appears three times with variant spelling מרטא — likely scribal variants of the Aramaic name Martha.

verses.literal: And it happened that Yeshua prayed in a certain place when he entered into a tower one and there was and there was there [whose] name [was] her sister Marta Marta Marta and she said to him help me lord you you [are] the bread to them the bread to them
And he said to them say our Father your name will be sanctified and in your kingdom we will come
verses.amplified: And he said to them: Say — Our Father, your name will be set apart [or: hallowed, sanctified], and into your kingdom we will come [or: enter].
work: ואמר (אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H561 'something said', H563 'a lamb'. Chose H559 because the form ואמר with ו-consecutive + prefix is a standard narrative verb 'and he said', fitting the context of someone instructing others.
להם (הם): Candidates: H1992 'they/them', H1990 'Ham (place)', H1991 'abundance'. Chose H1992 because ל + הם = 'to them', standard indirect object in a speech introduction.

verses.literal: Give to us bread [of] our portion day day
verses.amplified: Give to us [the] bread of our allotted portion [or: our prescribed need], day [by] day.
work: תן: The candidate listed is H8565 'sea-serpent', but the consonants תן here clearly represent the imperative of נתן (H5414, 'to give'). The Strong's list provided is incomplete; תן is the standard masculine singular imperative of נתן. Context demands 'give' as the sentence is a petition for bread.
לחם: Candidates: H3898 'to feed/battle', H3899 'bread/food', H3901 'battle'. Chose H3899 because the petition context ('give to us') demands a noun meaning food/bread, not battle or a verb.
ambiguities: חוקינו — from חק (H2706), meaning 'statute, prescribed portion, allotment.' This could mean 'our daily prescribed portion' or 'our statutory need.' The word emphasizes that the amount asked for is not excess but what is lawfully apportioned.

verses.literal: And release to us all our sins for we are releasing them to all our debtors and not bring us to trial
verses.amplified: And set aside [or: release, forgive] for us all our sins, for we [ourselves] are releasing [or: forgiving] them to all who are indebted to us. And do not bring us into trial [or: testing].
work: והנח (נח): The candidate listed is H5146 'Noah (the patriarch).' However, the consonants נח also represent the root of H5117 (נוח, 'to rest, set down, leave, release'). The hiphil form הנח means 'to set down, leave, release.' Context demands a verb of forgiveness/release, not a proper name.
כי: Candidates: H3587 'a brand/scar', H3588 'conjunction: for, because, that'. Chose H3588 because it introduces the reason clause ('for we are releasing them').

ואל (אל): Candidates: H408 'not (deprecative negation)', H410 'God/mighty', H413 'to/near'. Chose H408 because ואל + imperfect תביאנו forms a negative petition ('do not bring us'), standard Hebrew syntax for a request not to do something.
ambiguities: מחוייבינו — a post-biblical Hebrew form meaning 'those who are obligated/indebted to us.' The root חוב (to be indebted/guilty) is primarily found in later Hebrew and Aramaic.
לנסיון — from נסה/נסיון meaning 'trial, test, temptation.' The word could mean a trial of faith, a test of character, or an ordeal.

verses.literal: And he said to them which this from you there is to him a friend and he will go to him in half the night and he will say to him my beloved lend to me loaves bread three
verses.amplified: And he said to them: Which [one] among you has a friend, and he goes to him at midnight, and says to him — My beloved [or: dear friend], lend me three loaves of bread,
work: ואמר (אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H563 'a lamb'. Chose H559 — narrative speech formula.

אי: Candidates: H335 'where/which', H336 'not', H337 'alas', H338 'wild creature', H339 'island'. Chose H335 because אי זה together form the interrogative 'which one?' — a standard Hebrew compound interrogative.
זה: Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep'. Chose H2088 because אי זה = 'which one' is a well-attested interrogative phrase.
בחצי (חצי): Candidates: H2677 'half/middle', H2678 'arrow'. Chose H2677 because 'in the half of the night' = midnight makes perfect sense; 'in the arrow of the night' does not.
לחם: Candidates: H3899 'bread', H3898 'to battle'. Chose H3899 — the request is for food to serve a guest.

שלשה: Candidates: H8030 'Shilshah (name)', H8031 'Shalishah (place)', H7716 'sheep'. The consonants שלשה most naturally represent the number three (H7969, שְׁלֹשָׁה). The candidates listed do not include the numeral, but the consonants are identical to the common numeral. Context demands a number modifying loaves.

ככרות: The candidate listed (H7327 'Ruth') relates only to the sub-consonants רות. The full consonants ככרות represent the plural of ככר (H3603, 'a round loaf, talent, plain'). In context of bread, 'loaves/rounds' is the clear reading.

verses.literal: For my beloved came from the road to me and there is not to me what I am able to set before him
verses.amplified: For my beloved [or: dear friend] has come to me from the road [or: journey], and I have nothing that I can set before him.
work: כי: Candidates: H3587 'brand/scar', H3588 'for/because'. Chose H3588 — introduces the reason for the request.
מהדרך (דרך): Candidates: H1869 'to tread', H1870 'a road/journey'. Chose H1870 because מן + הדרך = 'from the road/journey,' describing where the friend came from.
ואין (אין): Candidates: H369 'non-entity/negative particle', H370 'where?', H371 'is it not?'. Chose H369 because ואין לי = 'and there is not to me' = 'I have nothing.'
מה: Candidates: H4100 'what?', H4101 same. Chose H4100 — here functioning as a relative 'what [thing]' rather than interrogative.
ambiguities: 2אוכל — the '2' prefix appears to be a scribal or editorial mark. The consonants אוכל could be from אכל (H398, 'to eat/food') or from יכל (H3201, 'to be able'). In context, 'what I am able to set before him' makes better sense than 'food to set before him,' since the whole point is that he has no food. Chose 'I am able' (H3201).
להניח — from נוח (H5117), hiphil infinitive 'to set, place, lay down.' In context it means 'to set [food] before him.'

verses.translation: And he answered him from inside: Do not trouble [or: distress, bother] me! Look — the door [is] shut, and my children are now in bed [or: on the sleeping mat]. I am not able to get up to give you the morsel [or: piece of bread].
words: in bed / on the sleeping mat

translation_notes: והוא: Candidates: H1931 'he', H1932 'he (Aramaic)', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. Chose H1931 as the pronoun 'and he' introducing the subject of the response.

ענה: Candidates: H6030 'to respond/answer', H6031 'to depress/afflict', H6032 'to answer (Aramaic)', H6033 'to depress (Aramaic)', H6034 'Anah'. Chose H6030 because 'he answered him' is the natural speech-report verb here.
אל: Candidates: H408 'not (prohibitive)', H410 'God/mighty', H413 'to'. Chose H408 because with the imperfect תצערני it forms 'do not trouble me'.
הנה: Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither', H2009 'behold/lo', H5089 'lamentation'. Chose H2009 because 'behold, the door is shut' is a natural exclamatory introduction.

ובני: Candidates: H1137 'Bani (name)', H1138 'Bunni (name)', H5204 'lamentation'. None of these fit. The form is ו + בני 'and my sons/children' from בן (H1121). Chose H1121 with 1cs pronominal suffix.
הם: Candidates: H1990 'Ham (place)', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 because 'my children, they [are] now in bed' requires the pronoun.

במטה: Candidates: H4294 'rod/staff/tribe', H4295 'downward/below', H4296 'bed/sleeping mat', H4297 'distortion', H4298 'expansion'. Chose H4296 because 'in bed' is the natural image — children sleeping at midnight.
לקום: Candidates: H3946 'Lakkum (place)', H6965 'to rise', H6966 'to rise (Aramaic)'. Chose H6965 as the infinitive 'to rise/get up', which makes sense as the man's excuse.
הפת: Candidates: H6595 'a bit/morsel', H6596 'a hole/hinge'. Chose H6595 because 'to give you the morsel/bread-piece' completes the narrative about food.
textual_notes: תצערני — no Strong's candidates listed. This is from the root צער 'to be small/to trouble/distress', a post-biblical Hebrew form. The meaning 'do not trouble/bother me' is clear from context.
איניני — no Strong's candidates listed. This is a compound negative form אין + אני 'I am not' (literally 'there-is-not-I'), a colloquial Hebrew construction meaning 'I am unable'.

verses.literal: And he answered to-him from-within: Do not trouble-me. Behold the door [is] shut and my-children they [are] now in-bed. I-am-not-able to-rise to-give to-you the bread-piece.

verses.translation: And if he persists in asking, I say to you: even if he did not rise on account of his friendship [or: love] — his prayer will teach us. He taught: When you come [in prayer], it will be given. And give [forgiveness]. And [each] day [release us] from all our debts. [Do not bring us] into trial. To them [he said]: Which [of you], at midnight, [would say] 'Lend me — loan me three loaves'? You will rise and give to him according to his need.
words: on account of / for the sake of

translation_notes: ואם: Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/although'. Chose H518 as the conditional 'and if'.
הוא: Candidates: H1931 'he', H1933 'to be', H1934 'to exist'. Chose H1931 as the subject pronoun 'he'.
אני: Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'ship/fleet'. Chose H589 because 'I say to you' requires the first person pronoun.
אומר: Candidate H201 'Omar (name)'. But this is clearly a participle of אמר (H559) 'saying/I say'. The name Omar is irrelevant here.
שאם: ש + אם. Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if'. Chose H518: 'that if' introducing the conditional clause.
בעד: Candidates: H1157 'on account of/for', plus עד candidates. Chose H1157 because 'on account of his love/friendship' explains the motivation.
ויום: Candidates: H3117 'day', H3118 'day (Aramaic)'. Chose H3117. This appears to be a fragment of the prayer teaching: 'and [each] day'.
להם: Candidates: H3859 'to rankle/burn', H1992 'they/them'. Chose H1992 as 'to them', indicating the audience of the teaching.
בחצות: H2676 'the middle (of the night)'. Only one candidate; 'at midnight' is clear.
ככר: Candidates: H3603 'a round/loaf/talent', H3604 'a talent (Aramaic)', H3733 'ram/meadow', H3734 'a cor/measure'. Chose H3603 because 'a loaf' fits the bread-lending parable.
textual_notes: This section appears to be a composite or marginal annotation that interweaves commentary on the parable with fragments of prayer instruction. The text flow is disrupted, with what appears to be a teaching gloss ('his prayer will teach us, he taught...') followed by abbreviated prayer elements ('it will be given, and give, and day, from all our debts, in trial') and then a return to the midnight parable ('to them: which, at midnight, lend me...').
בהתמדה — no Strong's candidate. This is from the root תמד 'to persist/persevere' in a hitpael nominal form, meaning 'with persistence/perseverance'.

תפילתו תלמד אותנו לימד — this sequence is syntactically unusual. It could be read as: 'his prayer will teach us — he taught [saying]:' followed by abbreviated prayer elements. Or it could be a marginal gloss that crept into the text.
הלויני and הלוני appear to be variant forms of the same request 'lend me', possibly representing two manuscript traditions preserved side by side.
ג׳ שלש — the numeral abbreviation ג׳ (gimel = 3) followed by the spelled-out שלש 'three' is redundant, suggesting a scribal gloss or clarification.
מחייובנו — no Strong's candidate. This appears to be from חוב/חיב 'to be obligated/indebted' with 1cp suffix: 'our debts/obligations'.

verses.literal: And if he in-persistence [is] asking, I say to-you that-if not he-rose and-not on-account-of his-love... His-prayer will-teach us. He-taught: In-coming, it-will-be-given. And give. And day from-all our-debtors. In-trial. To-them: which at-midnight lend-me loan-me a-loaf three. You-will-rise and-give to-him according-to the-need for-him.

verses.translation: Ask, and it will be given to you. Seek [or: search diligently], and you will find. Knock [or: strike the door], and it will be opened for you.

translation_notes: שאלו: The candidates listed (H431 'lo', H432 'if') refer to אלו only. But שאלו is the imperative plural of שאל (H7592) 'to ask/inquire'. Chose H7592 as this clearly means 'ask!'.
ויפתח: Candidate H3316 'Jiphtach/Jephthah (name)'. But this is ו + יפתח, the niphal/pual imperfect of פתח (H6605) 'to open': 'it will be opened'. The proper name is irrelevant here.
textual_notes: תקעו — from תקע (H8628) 'to clap, strike, blow (a horn), thrust'. In context, this means 'knock/strike [on a door]', extending the door-parable imagery. The verb is commonly associated with blowing a horn, but the physical sense of striking fits the door context.

verses.literal: Ask and it-will-be-given to-you. Seek and you-will-find. Knock and it-will-be-opened to-you.

verses.translation: For every person who asks receives, and whoever seeks finds, and to whoever knocks, [the door] will be opened for him.

translation_notes: כי: Candidates: H3587 'brand/scar', H3588 'for/because/that'. Chose H3588 as the causal conjunction 'for' explaining the preceding imperative.
איש: Candidates: H376 'a man/individual', H377 'to act as a man'. Chose H376 as the noun 'every person'.
ש<ואל: The < mark suggests textual damage. The reading is שׁואל from שאל (H7592) 'who asks'. The ש functions as a relative pronoun.

מוצא: Candidates: H4161 'a going forth/exit/source', H4162 'Motsa (name)'. But in context this is the active participle of מצא (H4672) 'to find': 'finds'. The form מוצא as participle fits the pattern of the other clauses (asking→receiving, seeking→finding).
ומי: H4310 'who'. The interrogative/indefinite 'whoever' in the pattern of general truths.
שמבקש: ש + מבקש from בקש (H1245) 'to seek/search'. The ש is a relative pronoun: 'who seeks'.
textual_notes: ש<ואל — the < character in the consonantal text suggests damage or an editorial mark. The intended reading שואל 'who asks' is clear from context.

מוצא — could be the noun H4161 'a going forth/source/product' or the participle of מצא 'finds'. The parallel structure (asks→receives, seeks→finds, knocks→opened) strongly favors the verbal participle 'finds'.
פתחו — this could be parsed as 3mp 'they open' or as a passive/impersonal construction 'it is opened for him'. Both yield essentially the same meaning.

verses.literal: For every man who-asks receives, and-who that-seeks finds, and-to-who that-knocks they-open to-him.

verses.translation: Which [one] among you, if his son asks his father for bread [or: food, grain], would give him a stone? And if [he asks for] a fish, would give him a serpent [or: snake]?

translation_notes: אם (consonants אם): Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether'. Chose H518 because this introduces a conditional rhetorical question about what a father would do.

לחם (consonants לחם): Candidates: H3898 'to feed/battle', H3899 'bread/food', H3900 'bread', H3901 'battle'. Chose H3899 because the passage contrasts edible things (bread, fish) with harmful substitutes (stone, serpent).
אבן (consonants אבן): Candidates: H68 'a stone', H69 'a stone', H70 'a pair of stones/potter's wheel'. Chose H68 because a single stone is the natural inedible counterpart to bread in this contrast.

נחש (consonants נחש): Candidates: H5172 'to hiss/prognosticate', H5173 'incantation', H5174 'copper', H5175 'a snake', H5176 'Nachash (proper name)'. Chose H5175 because a snake is the natural dangerous counterpart to a fish — both are elongated creatures, one edible, one harmful.

verses.literal: Which from you if he asks bread from his father will he give to him a stone and if a fish will he give to him a serpent

verses.translation: And if [he asks for] an egg, would he give him a scorpion?

translation_notes: ואם (consonants אם): Candidates: H517 'mother', H518 'if/whether'. Chose H518 because this continues the conditional pattern from section 1.

verses.literal: And if an egg will he give to him a scorpion

verses.translation: If [it is] so that you do not trust in evil [or: wickedness] but [rather] you give good gifts to your children, how much more [will] our Father in the heavens give the Spirit [or: breath, wind] to whoever asks Him!

translation_notes: אם (consonants אם): H517 'mother' vs H518 'if/conditional'. Chose H518 because this introduces a conditional logical argument.

ברע (consonants רע): Candidates: H1298 'Bera (proper name)', H7451 'evil/bad', H7452 'a crash/noise', H7453 'associate/companion', H7454 'a thought', H7455 'badness'. Chose H7451 because the passage contrasts the evil nature of the audience with their still-good gift-giving, building a fortiori argument.
מה/וכמה: The phrase כ מה וכמה is an idiomatic Hebrew expression meaning 'how much more' — a qal va-chomer (a fortiori) argument. Both instances of מה read as H4100 'how much/what'.

הרוח (consonants רוח): Candidates: H7304 'to breathe freely', H7305 'room/relief', H7306 'to blow/smell', H7307 'wind/breath/spirit', H7308 'wind/spirit'. Chose H7307 because the definite article marks this as a specific noun — 'the spirit' — and it is the gift the heavenly father gives, fitting the climax of the argument.
textual_notes: שב<מים contains a damaged/unclear consonant marked with <. Reading as שבשמים ('that in the heavens') based on context — our Father who is in the heavens.

The phrase אם לא שלא is unusual and could be parsed as 'if not ... that not' (double negation yielding a positive sense: 'even though you are evil') or as a concessive 'even though'. The logic requires a concessive reading: despite being evil, you still give good gifts.
הרוח could be 'the wind', 'the breath', or 'the Spirit' — the consonants and article do not disambiguate the theological sense.

verses.literal: If not that not you trust in evil surely you give gifts good to your sons how much and how much our father in the heavens that he gives the spirit to whoever asks him

verses.translation: And it happened [that] he was driving out the adversary [or: Satan], and the mute [one] spoke, and the peoples were amazed.

translation_notes: מגרש (consonants מגרש): Candidates: H4054 'suburb/open country', H1644 'to drive out/expel'. Chose H1644 (participle form: 'driving out') because the context describes expelling an adversary — a suburb/open country makes no sense here.

השטן (consonants שטן): Candidates: H7853 'to attack/accuse', H7854 'an opponent/Satan'. Chose H7854 because the article ה prefixed indicates a noun — 'the adversary/Satan' — and this is being expelled.

האלם (consonants אלם): Candidates: H481 'to tie fast/be tongue-tied', H482 'silence', H483 'speechless/mute'. Chose H483 because with the article ה it functions as a substantive adjective — 'the mute one' — who then speaks.

דבר (consonants דבר): Candidates: H1696 'to speak/arrange words', H1697 'a word/matter', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. Chose H1696 because the mute one performs the action of speaking after the expulsion.
textual_notes: The syntax is ambiguous: 'driving out the adversary' could mean he was expelling a demonic spirit called 'the adversary' from the mute person, or that 'the adversary' is in apposition to what made the person mute. The result is the same: the mute person speaks after the expulsion.

verses.literal: And it was [that] he was driving out the adversary the mute [one] spoke and the peoples were astonished

verses.translation: And some [or: a portion] of them said, By Baal Zebub [lord of the fly], the prince [or: ruler] of the demons, he drives out the demons.

translation_notes: ומקצת (consonants קצת): Candidates: H7117 'a termination/portion', H7118 'portion'. Chose H7117 because 'a portion of them' = 'some of them', fitting the context of a subset of the crowd speaking.
מהם (consonants הם): Candidates: H1990 'Ham (place)', H1991 'abundance', H1992 'they'. Chose H1992 because מ + הם = 'from them', a standard partitive construction.
בבעל (consonants בעל): Candidates: H1166 'to be master', H1167 'a master/owner', H1168 'Baal'. Chose H1168 because 'Baal Zebub' is a known compound name for a pagan deity.
שר (consonants שר): Candidates: H8269 'a head person/ruler', H8270 'a string/cord'. Chose H8269 because 'prince of the demons' describes the rank attributed to Baal Zebub.
מגרש: Same as section 4 — H1644 'to drive out/expel', as the context is about casting out demons.
textual_notes: ה<דים appears twice with a damaged/unclear consonant marked <. Based on context (beings that are driven out, associated with Satan/Baal Zebub), this likely reads השדים ('the demons') from שד (H7700 'a demon').

verses.literal: And a portion from them said by Baal Zebub prince of the demons he drives out the demons

verses.translation: And others, testing [or: putting to the test] him, asked him [for] a sign from the heavens.

translation_notes: אות (consonants אות): Candidates: H225 'to come/assent', H226 'a signal/sign/omen'. Chose H226 because they are requesting visible proof — a sign from heaven.
מן (consonants מן): Candidates: H4478 'manna', H4479 'who/what', H4480 'from/out of', H4481 'from', H4482 'a musical chord'. Chose H4480 because the preposition 'from' fits: a sign from the heavens.
textual_notes: ה<מים contains a damaged consonant marked <. Given the context of requesting a heavenly sign, this almost certainly reads השמים ('the heavens') from שמים (H8064).

verses.literal: And others testing him asked him a sign from the heavens

verses.translation: And Yeshua, as one who understood [or: discerned] their intentions [or: deeds], said to them: Every kingdom that is divided [against itself] will not stand, and house will fall upon house.

translation_notes: וישוע (consonants ישוע): Candidates: H3442 'Jeshua', H3443 'Jeshua'. Both refer to the same name; chose H3442 as the primary entry.

כמבין (consonants בין): Candidates: H995 'to separate mentally/understand', H996 'between', H997 'between'. Chose H995 because כ + מבין = 'as one who understands/discerns' — a hiphil participle of בין with כ prefix.

אמר (consonants אמר): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 'to say', H561 'something said', H562 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer'. Chose H559 because the context is direct speech — he said to them.

שחלק (consonants חלק): Candidates: H2505 'to divide/apportion', H2506 'allotment', H2507-H2510 various. Chose H2505 because ש + חלק = 'that is divided' — a verb in relative clause describing the kingdom.
על (consonants על): Candidates: H5920 'the top/God', H5921 'upon/against', H5922 'upon', H5923 'a yoke'. Chose H5921 because 'house falls upon house' describes collapse and internal conflict.
textual_notes: ]להם[ is marked with brackets in the source, indicating it is an editorial insertion. It likely reads 'against itself/them' to complete the sense of a kingdom divided against itself.

לשמוע: H8051 is a personal name 'Shammua,' but ל + שמוע is clearly the infinitive construct of שמע 'to hear,' fitting 'to hear the wisdom of.' The ל prefix marks purpose.
שלמה: Candidates: H8008 'dress,' H8009 'Salmah,' H8010 'Shelomoh (David's successor),' H8011 'retribution.' Context of wisdom and a queen visiting identifies H8010 Solomon.
והנה: Candidates: H2007 'themselves,' H2008 'hither,' H2009 'lo!/behold.' The exclamatory 'and behold' (H2009) fits the dramatic announcement that follows.
מקצות: Not in candidates but recognizable as מן + קצות, plural construct of קצה 'end/extremity.' 'From the ends of.'
בכאן: A post-biblical Hebrew locative 'here/in this place.' The candidate H575 אן 'where' is the base, with prefix ב and כ. Reading as 'in here.'
מ<למה: The < indicates damage. Context and parallel with שלמה above strongly suggest מ + שלמה 'than Solomon,' with the שׁ partially lost.
textual_notes: The word באה is listed only as H872 'entrance to a building' but contextually must be the 3fs perfect of בוא 'to come.' The Strong's database appears incomplete for this verbal form.
מ<למה has a damaged letter indicated by <. Reconstruction as מ+שלמה (than Solomon) is based on the parallel with the earlier שלמה and the comparative מן prefix.

verses.literal: And she will punish them. [The] queen [of] Sheba came from [the] ends [of] the earth to hear [the] wisdom [of] Shelomoh, and behold there is in here [one] greater than Sh[e]l[o]moh.

verses.translation: The men of Nineveh will rise up in the judgment against this generation [or: family, clan] and will condemn it, because they made repentance [or: turning back] on account of the proclamation of Jonah — and behold, here [is one] greater than Jonah.

translation_notes: אנשי: Construct plural of איש 'man.' 'Men of.'
יקומו: 3mp imperfect of קום 'to rise.' 'They will rise.'

בדין: Candidates: H1777 'sail direct,' H1778 'to judge,' H1779 'judgment,' H1780 same, H1781 'judge,' H1782 same. With prefix ב, H1779 'in judgment' produces the most coherent image — rising up in a judicial proceeding.
עם: Candidates: H5971 'people,' H5973 'with/against.' As a preposition following 'rise in judgment,' H5973 'with/against' is the natural reading.
המשפחה: Candidates: H4940 'family/clan/generation,' H8198 'female slave.' In context of a judicial comparison between groups, H4940 'family/generation' fits — referring to the current generation.
עשו: H6215 'Esau' is the only candidate, but contextually this is clearly 3mp perfect of עשה 'to do/make.' 'They did/made repentance.'
דרישת: Construct form of דרישה, from root דרש 'to seek/inquire/preach.' 'The preaching/proclamation of.'
יונה (first): Candidates: H3123 'dove,' H3124 'Jonah.' Context of Nineveh and preaching clearly identifies H3124 Jonah the prophet.
מיונה: Same candidates. מ prefix is comparative 'than.' H3124 Jonah fits the parallel structure.
textual_notes: המשפחה could be 'family/clan' (H4940) or parsed as ה+שפחה 'the female slave' (H8198). The judicial context of generational comparison makes H4940 'family/generation' the clear choice.
עשו shares consonants with H6215 Esau but is contextually the 3mp perfect of עשה. The verb form is unmistakable in context.

verses.literal: Men of Nineveh will rise in judgment with this family and will punish her, for they did repentance on account of [the] preaching of Yonah, and behold in here [one] more great than Yonah.

verses.translation: The one who lights the lamp does not place it in a hidden spot [or: concealed place] and under a cover — rather, he places it upon the lampstand, so that those who enter the house may see the light.

translation_notes: המדליק: Hiphil participle with article, from root דלק 'to burn/kindle.' 'The one who lights.'
העששית: Post-biblical Hebrew word for 'lamp/lantern,' from root עשש. Not in Strong's as a standard entry.
נחבא: Niphal participle of חבא 'to hide.' 'Hidden/concealed.'
ותחת: Candidates: H8478 'underneath/below,' H8480 'Tachath (proper name).' With ו conjunction, H8478 'and under' is the only coherent reading following 'hidden place.'
רק: Candidates: H7534 'emaciated,' H7535 'only/merely/rather,' H7536 'spittle.' H7535 as an adversative adverb 'rather/only' fits the contrast between hiding and displaying the lamp.
על: Candidates: H5920 'the top,' H5921 'upon/over,' H5923 'yoke.' H5921 'upon' fits placing a lamp on a stand.
בעבור: H5668 'on account of/in order that' fits the purpose clause.
בבית: Candidates: H1004 'house,' H1006 'Bajith.' H1004 'house' is the natural reading for a domestic setting.
הנר: H5369 is 'Ner, an Israelite,' but הנר with article is clearly 'the lamp/light' from נר (lamp). Strong's H5216 would be the proper entry but was not listed among candidates.
שהנכנסין: Relative ש + article ה + נכנסין (entering ones), from root כנס. The -ין ending is a Mishnaic Hebrew plural participle form.
יראו: 3mp imperfect of ראה 'to see.' 'They will see.'
textual_notes: הנר: The only candidate given is H5369 'Ner, an Israelite,' but this is clearly the common noun נר 'lamp/light' with the article. Strong's H5216 would apply but was not in the candidate list.

verses.literal: The one who lights the lamp is not placing it in a place hidden and under a covering, only placing it upon the lampstand in order that those entering into [the] house will see the light.

verses.translation: The lamp [or: lantern] of your body is your eye. If your eye is sound [or: whole, complete, blameless], your entire body will be filled with light. But if your eye is evil [or: bad, malicious], your body will be darkness [or: in the dark].

translation_notes: הוא: Candidates: H1931 'he/it,' H1933 'to be,' H1934 'to exist.' As the copula linking 'lamp of your body' to 'your eye,' H1931 'it [is]' is the natural reading.
אם (both): Candidates: H517 'mother,' H518 'if/whether.' As the opening of a conditional clause, H518 'if' is unmistakable.

תמים: Candidates: H8549 'entire/whole/blameless,' H8550 'perfections (Thummim).' Describing an eye's quality, H8549 'whole/sound/complete' makes a coherent physical and moral image — an eye that is sound lets in light.

אבל: Candidates include H56 'to bewail,' H57 'lamenting,' H58 'meadow,' H61 'nay/truly/yet.' As an adversative conjunction introducing the contrasting condition, H61 'but/yet' is the only coherent reading.

רע: Candidates: H7451 'bad/evil,' H7452 'crash/noise,' H7453 'associate,' H7454 'thought,' H7455 'badness.' Describing an eye in contrast to 'whole/sound,' H7451 'evil/bad' produces the clearest antithesis.
ועששית: Post-biblical 'lamp/lantern' with conjunction ו. Same word as section 3.
גופך: 'Your body' — post-biblical Hebrew גוף 'body' with 2ms suffix.
עינך: 'Your eye' — עין 'eye' with 2ms suffix.
מאיר: Hiphil participle of אור 'to give light/shine.' 'Illuminated/giving light.'

verses.literal: And [the] lamp of your body it [is] your eye. If your eye will be whole, all your body will be illuminated. But if your eye will be evil, your body will be dark.

verses.translation: Therefore, take care that your light does not become dark, and your whole body will shine. And when there is no murky [or: foggy, shadowed] portion in it at all, it will radiate light like a lamp illuminating [you] with [its] brilliance.

translation_notes: לכן: כן candidates: H3651 'thus/therefore,' H3652 'so,' H3653 'stand,' H3654 'gnat.' With ל prefix, לכן = 'therefore' (H3651).
שמור: Candidates: H8053 'Shamur (name),' H4171 'to alter.' But שמור is clearly the imperative of שמר 'to guard/keep/take care.' The context of an exhortation demands the verb.
שנרך: ש (relative/that) + נר (lamp/light) + ך (your). 'That your light.'
תחשך: 2ms/3fs imperfect of חשך 'to darken.' 'Will darken / becomes dark.'
וכאשר: Candidates for אשר: H834 'who/which/when.' With prefix וכ, reading 'and when/as' — introducing a temporal/conditional clause.
חלק: Candidates: H2505 'to apportion,' H2506 'portion/part,' H2507-H2510 various. As a noun following 'there will not be in it,' H2506 'part/portion' fits — 'no portion of darkness.'
ערפליי: From ערפל 'thick darkness/fog/gloom' with adjectival suffix. 'Foggy/murky/dark.'

כשלו: Likely כ + שלו or כל + שלו. Candidates for שלו: H7958 'quail,' H7959 'security,' H7960 'fault,' H7961 'tranquil.' However, in context כלו (all of it) makes far more sense — reading כ as corrupted from כל, or this as כלו 'all of it/the whole of it.' A body with no dark portion → all of it shines.
יאיר: H2971 'Jair (name)' is the only candidate, but this is clearly the hiphil imperfect 3ms of אור 'to give light/shine.' Strong's H215 would apply.
textual_notes: כשלו is ambiguous: could be כ+שלו 'as/like its wholeness/tranquility' or a corruption of כלו 'all of it.' The latter reading ('all of it will shine') produces the most coherent image in context of a body with no dark portion shining completely.
יאיר: The only Strong's candidate given is H2971 (Jair, a name), but contextually this is the hiphil imperfect of אור 'to illuminate.' The verbal reading is certain from context.
שמור: Listed candidates are H8053 (a name) and H4171 (to alter), but this is unmistakably the imperative of שמר 'to guard.'

verses.literal: Therefore guard that your light not darken, and all your body will give light, and when not will be in it a part foggy, all of it will give light like a lamp the illuminating.

verses.translation: And while he was speaking, a certain Pharisee [or: separated one] asked him to eat with him. And he entered the house, sat down, and reclined [at the table].

translation_notes: ובעוד: עוד candidates: H5749 'to testify,' H5750 'still/while/again,' H5751 same. With ב prefix and ו conjunction, 'and while/during' (H5750) fits the temporal clause.
שהוא: הוא candidates: H1931 'he,' H1933 'to be.' As subject of the clause 'while he was speaking,' H1931 'he' is natural.

מדבר: Candidates: H4057 'desert/speech,' H1696 'to speak,' H1697 'word.' As a participle 'speaking' (from דבר, piel participle), this fits 'while he was speaking.' H4057 includes 'speech' in its range but the verbal participle reading is primary.
אחד: Candidates: H258 'to unify,' H259 'one/first.' As an adjective modifying 'Pharisee,' H259 'one/a certain' is the clear reading.
בבית: Candidates: H1004 'house,' H1006 'Bajith (place).' Domestic context of a meal — H1004 'house.'
בקשהו: Root בקש 'to seek/request' + 3ms object suffix. 'Requested him / asked him.'
פרוש: From root פרש 'to separate.' A Pharisee — one who is separated/set apart.
והסב: Root סבב 'to turn/surround' — hiphil 'to recline (at table).' Common in Mishnaic Hebrew for reclining at a meal.
textual_notes: מדבר shares consonants with H4057 'desert/wilderness/speech.' In context of 'while he was [doing something],' the piel participle of דבר 'speaking' is the only coherent reading.

verses.literal: And while that he [was] speaking, requested him a Pharisee one that he would eat with him, and he entered into [the] house, sat and reclined.
And the Pharisee said in his heart why this he is not washing his hands at the meal of the morning
verses.amplified: And the Pharisee [or: separated one] said in his heart: Why [is] this [one] not washing his hands at the morning meal [or: breakfast]?
work: אמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H563 'a lamb'. Chose H559 — the Pharisee is speaking/thinking internally.
זה: Candidates: H2088 'this/that', H2089 'a sheep'. Chose H2088 because 'why is this one not washing' is coherent; 'why is a sheep not washing' is not.

הבקר (בקר): Candidates: H1239 'to inspect', H1241 'cattle', H1242 'morning'. Chose H1242 because בסעודת הבקר = 'at the meal of the morning' = breakfast, which fits the scene of a meal with hand-washing customs.
ambiguities: פרוש — this word means 'separated one' and is the Hebrew term for a Pharisee. Not in the standard Strong's numbering as it is a post-biblical formation from פרש (H6567, 'to separate').

verses.literal: And our lord said to him Pharisees now you are purifying what [is] from outside [the] goblet and from the bowl and what [is] on [the] inside of you it [is] heart evil and theft
verses.amplified: And our lord said to him: Pharisees [or: separated ones] — now you purify [or: cleanse] what is on the outside of [the] goblet and of the bowl, but what is on your inside — it is an evil [or: wicked] heart and theft [or: robbery].
work: אמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H563 'a lamb'. Chose H559 — speech verb in narrative.

אתם: The candidate listed is H864 'Etham (place).' However, the consonants אתם standardly represent the 2nd person masculine plural pronoun 'you' (H859). Context requires the pronoun: 'you are purifying.'
הוא: Candidates: H1931 'he/it', H1933 'to be'. Chose H1931 — functioning as a relative/demonstrative 'that which is' outside/inside.
ומן (מן): Candidates: H4478 'manna', H4480 'from/out of'. Chose H4480 — 'and from the bowl' parallels 'from outside the goblet.'

רע: Candidates: H7451 'evil/bad', H7452 'noise', H7453 'associate/friend', H7455 'badness'. Chose H7451 because 'evil heart' contrasts the inner reality with the outer cleansing, and pairs naturally with 'theft.'
ambiguities: The < symbol before הוא appears to be a scribal marker, possibly indicating a relative pronoun construction ('that which is'). The phrase מה <הוא מחוץ means 'what is on the outside.'
וגניבה — from גנב (H1589, 'to steal'). The noun form גניבה ('theft, stolen goods') is post-biblical but clearly derived from the biblical root.

verses.literal: Fools [did] not he who made what [is] from outside make what [is] on the inside
verses.amplified: Fools! Did not the one who made what is on the outside also make what is on the inside?
work: מי: H4310 'who?' — here functioning as an implied rhetorical question: 'the one who made the outside, did he not [also] make the inside?'
לא: Candidates: H3808 'not', H3809 'not (Aramaic)'. Chose H3808 — standard Hebrew negation in a rhetorical question expecting an affirmative answer.
ambiguities: The syntax is somewhat compressed. The sentence can be parsed as: 'Fools! He who made what is on the outside — did he not [also] make what is on the inside?' The word order places מי שעשה ('the one who made') before the negation לא עשה ('did he not make'), creating a rhetorical question that asserts the same maker crafted both exterior and interior.

verses.literal: Therefore give in righteousness what [is] extra to you and all the things will be to you pure
verses.amplified: Therefore, give in charitable righteousness [or: as charity] what is surplus [or: left over] to you, and all things will be pure [or: clean] for you.
work: לכן (כן): Candidates: H3651 'so/therefore', H3652 'so (Aramaic)', H3653 'stand/pedestal', H3654 'gnat'. Chose H3651 because ל + כן = 'therefore,' a standard logical connector following the preceding argument.

בצדקה: Candidates: H6665 'beneficence', H6666 'righteousness/justice/charity'. Chose H6666 because in later Hebrew צדקה carries the specific meaning of charitable giving, which fits the imperative 'give.'
מה: H4100 — here functioning as a relative pronoun: 'that which is surplus.'
ambiguities: <יותר — the < mark again appears to be a scribal/editorial marker. The root יתר (H3498) means 'to remain over, be surplus.' The form יותר means 'more, surplus, extra.' The instruction is to give away what remains beyond one's need.

verses.literal: Only woe to you Pharisees that you are tithing the mint and the rue and the cabbage and abandoning judgment and righteousness of YHWH these the things [are] fitting that they be done and not to leave them
verses.amplified: But woe to you, Pharisees [or: separated ones], for you tithe the mint and the rue and the cabbage [or: garden herb], yet you abandon justice [or: right judgment] and the righteousness of YHWH. These things are fitting [or: proper] to be done, and [the others] not to be left undone.
work: רק: Candidates: H7534 'emaciated', H7535 'only/merely/but', H7536 'spittle'. Chose H7535 because 'but/however woe to you' is a natural adversative transition after the positive instruction of section 9.
אוי: Candidates: H188 'woe/lamentation', H189 'Evi (name)'. Chose H188 — an interjection of woe, fitting the denunciation context.

מעשרים: The candidate listed is H6242 'twenty.' However, the consonants מעשרים clearly represent the piel participle plural of עשר (H6237, 'to tithe'). The מ prefix + עשר root = 'those who tithe / you are tithing.' Context demands tithing, not the number twenty.

והכרוב: Candidates: H3742 'cherub', H3743 'Kerub (place)'. The consonants כרוב in context of garden herbs alongside mint and rue more likely refer to a garden vegetable — כרוב meaning 'cabbage' in later Hebrew. This is not the same word as the biblical cherub despite identical consonants. Context of tithing garden produce demands a plant.

אלה: Candidates: H421 'bewail', H422 'imprecate', H423 'imprecation', H424 'oak tree', H426 'God'. However, the consonants אלה also represent H428 (אֵלֶּה, 'these'), the common demonstrative pronoun. Context demands 'these things are fitting,' not 'an oak' or 'God.'

שיעשו: The candidate listed is H3299 'Jaasu (name).' However, the consonants clearly represent ש + יעשו, where ש is the relative particle 'that' and יעשו is the 3mp imperfect of עשה (H6213, 'to do/make'). Context: 'fitting that they be done.'
שאתם: The candidate listed is H864 'Etham (place).' The consonants represent ש + אתם = 'that you' (relative particle + 2mp pronoun H859). Context requires 'that you are tithing.'
ambiguities: הנענא — 'mint.' This is a post-biblical Hebrew word (נענע) for the mint plant, not found in the standard Strong's lexicon. It is a loanword common in Mishnaic Hebrew.
והרודא — 'rue.' This is the plant Ruta graveolens, known in Mishnaic Hebrew as רודא. Not in standard Strong's.

והכרוב — while the consonants match H3742 'cherub,' the context of tithing herbs/garden produce strongly indicates the later Hebrew word כרוב meaning 'cabbage' or a garden vegetable. The identical consonants create a genuine ambiguity, but the surrounding botanical context resolves it.
ראויים — 'fitting, proper, worthy.' A post-biblical Hebrew adjective from the root ראה. Not in standard Strong's numbering.

verses.translation: How fitting [or: characteristic] of you, Pharisees, that you love to sit in the first [or: chief] seat in the houses of assembly [or: synagogues], and that they give you an abundance of greetings [or: peace] in the marketplace.

translation_notes: בכסא (B-K-S-ʾ): Candidates: H3677 'full moon/festival', H3678 'throne/seat'. Chose H3678 because sitting in the first seat/throne at assemblies is a coherent image of seeking honor.

שלום (Š-L-W-M): Candidates: H7965 'peace/welfare/greeting', H7966 'requital/fee', H7967 'Shallum (name)'. Chose H7965 because 'abundance of greetings' in the marketplace is a natural image of public honor-seeking.
textual_notes: ב<ער appears to have a damaged or unclear consonant (marked with <). The most likely reading is בשער 'in the gate/marketplace' or בשוער, but the exact consonant is uncertain. I have rendered it as 'in the marketplace' based on context.

ראוי could be read as 'fitting/worthy' (descriptive) or as an ironic 'woe' introduction parallel to the surrounding sections. The lack of אוי here suggests it is a different construction — perhaps sarcastic: 'How fitting for you.'

verses.literal: Fitting for you Pharisees that you love to sit in [the] seat first [in] houses [of] assemblies and that they give to you abundance [of] peace in the marketplace.

verses.translation: Woe to you, Pharisees! You are like graves [or: tombs] that are not visible, and people walk over [the] place without knowing [it].

translation_notes: אוי (ʾ-W-Y): Candidates: H188 'woe', H189 'Evi'. Chose H188 — exclamatory 'woe' fits the oracle pattern.
כמו (K-M-W): Only candidate H3644 'like/as'. Straightforward comparison.
למקום (L-M-Q-W-M): Candidates include H4725 'a place/standing' and H6965 'to rise'. Chose H4725 because 'walk to the place' forms a coherent image with the hidden graves.
textual_notes: The final clause שאינן יודעין is ambiguous: it could mean 'that are not known' (the graves/place are not known) or 'that they do not know' (the people are unaware). Both yield the same essential meaning: people unknowingly walk over hidden graves.

verses.literal: Woe to you Pharisees you [are] like the graves that are not seen and the people walk to [a] place that they do not know.

verses.translation: And one of the sages [or: experts] of the law answered and said, Rabbi, by saying these things you bring upon us dishonor [or: contempt].

translation_notes: וענה (W-ʿ-N-H): Candidates: H6030 'to answer/respond', H6031 'to afflict/depress', H6032-6034 variants. Chose H6030 because 'and answered' fits a dialogue context naturally.
הדת (H-D-T): Candidates: H1881 'royal edict/statute/law', H1882 same. Chose H1881 — 'the law' as in legal/religious code, fitting 'wise ones of the law.'
ואמר (W-ʾ-M-R): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560-564 variants. Chose H559 — standard verb 'and said.'

אלה: Candidates: H421 'bewail', H422 'adjure', H423 'imprecation', H424 'oak', H425 'Elah', H426 'God'. Here אלה functions as the demonstrative pronoun 'these' (common Hebrew usage), not any of the listed Strong's entries. This is a standard demonstrative not well captured by the candidates provided.
אתה (ʾ-T-H): Candidates: H857 'to arrive', H858 same, H859 'you'. Chose H859 because 'you do to us contempt' is the natural reading.
textual_notes: אלה as demonstrative 'these' does not have a perfect Strong's match among the candidates (which list bewail, adjure, oak, God, etc.). The demonstrative pronoun אלה is typically identified as H428, which was not provided. I read it as the demonstrative based on context.

verses.literal: And answered [one] from [the] wise ones [of] the law and said Rabbi in your saying these the things you do to us contempt.

verses.translation: And Yeshua said, Woe to you, sages of the law! Why do you load people down with burdens that they have no ability [or: strength] to carry, yet you yourselves are not willing to touch them with one finger of yours?

translation_notes: וישוע (W-Y-Š-W-ʿ): Candidates: H3442 'Jeshua', H3443 same. Chose H3442 — the proper name Yeshua/Jeshua.
אמר (ʾ-M-R): Candidates: H559 'to say', H560-564 variants. Chose H559.
אוי (ʾ-W-Y): Candidates: H188 'woe', H189 'Evi'. Chose H188.
למה (L-M-H): The prefix ל + H4100 מה 'what/why'. Reading as 'why' fits the accusatory context.
שאין (Š-ʾ-Y-N): The prefix ש 'that' + H369 אין 'there is not'. Standard negation in relative clause.
להם: Prepositional ל 'to' + הם 'them' (H1992). Not H3859 'to rankle' — 'to them' makes sense as 'they have no ability.'

לשאת (L-Š-ʾ-T): Could relate to H7612 'devastation', H7613 'elevation/scab', or this is ל + infinitive of נשא 'to lift/carry' (H5375, not listed). Context of carrying burdens strongly suggests the infinitive of נשא 'to carry/bear.'
באצבע (B-ʾ-Ṣ-B-ʿ): Candidates: H676 'finger', H677 same. Chose H676.
textual_notes: לשאת: The candidates provided (H7612 'devastation', H7613 'elevation') do not match the contextual meaning. This is almost certainly the infinitive construct of נשא (to carry/bear) with prefix ל, which would be H5375. The provided candidates for the root שאת do not capture this common parsing.

verses.literal: And Yeshua said woe to you wise ones [of] the law why you burden the people with burdens that there is not to them ability to bear and you not desired to touch them with finger one of yours.

verses.translation: Woe to you who hew out [or: carve] the tombs of the prophets — [the prophets] whom your fathers put to death!

translation_notes: אוי (ʾ-W-Y): Candidates: H188 'woe', H189 'Evi'. Chose H188.

המיתום: The candidate H3490 'orphan/bereaved' shares consonants י-ת-ו-ם but here the ה prefix + מית + ום reads as hiphil (causative) of מות 'to die' + suffix ם 'them' = 'they killed them.' Context of prophets being killed by fathers makes this the clear reading, not 'orphan.'

verses.literal: Woe to you hewers [of] graves [of] the prophets that your fathers killed them.

verses.translation: Truly, you bear witness that you have consented to [or: approved of] the deeds of your fathers — for they killed them, and you carve out their tombs.

translation_notes: באמת (B-ʾ-M-T): H571 'truth/certainty'. Prepositional phrase 'in truth' = truly.
במעשה (B-M-ʿ-Ś-H): Candidates: H4639 'action/deed/product', H6213 'to do/make'. Chose H4639 as the noun with prefix ב — 'in the deed of' your fathers.

שהחכמתם: The root חכם 'to be wise' in a causative or reflexive sense can mean 'to show agreement/approval' or 'to consent.' This is a distinctive reading — 'that you approved/consented to' the deeds of your fathers.
textual_notes: שהחכמתם is unusual. The root חכם typically means 'to be wise,' but here in context it seems to carry the sense of 'consenting/approving/taking counsel together.' This may be a Mishnaic Hebrew usage meaning 'you agreed with' or 'you showed approval for.'

verses.literal: In truth you testify that you agreed with [the] deed [of] your fathers that they killed them and you hewed their graves.

verses.translation: And because of this, the Wisdom of God said: Behold, I will send to them prophets and emissaries [or: apostles], and some of them they will kill and persecute [or: pursue].

translation_notes: ובעבור (W-B-ʿ-B-W-R): Candidates: H5668 'on account of / in order that', H5669 'stored grain'. Chose H5668 — 'on account of this' is contextually natural.
זה (Z-H): Candidates: H2088 'this', H2089 'sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose H2088 — demonstrative 'this.'

האל (H-ʾ-L): Candidates: H408/409 'not', H410 'God/mighty', H411/412 'these/those', H413 'to/near'. Chose H410 because 'the wisdom of God' is a coherent phrase and the ה prefix serves as the definite article on 'God.'
אמרה (ʾ-M-R-H): H565 'something said.' Here it functions as a feminine 3rd person verb 'she said' — the subject being חכמת (wisdom, feminine noun). This fits perfectly.
הנה (H-N-H): Candidates: H2007 'themselves', H2008 'hither/thither', H2009 'lo!/behold'. Chose H2009 — 'behold' introduces a prophetic declaration.
להם: Prepositional ל + הם (H1992 'them'), not H3859 'to rankle'. 'To them' is the natural reading.
ומהם: Prepositional מן 'from' + הם (H1992 'them'). 'And from them' = 'some of them.'

verses.literal: And on account of this [the] wisdom [of] God said behold I will send to them prophets and sent ones and from them they will kill and pursue.

verses.translation: So that the blood of all the prophets — from the day the world was created until now — will be required [or: demanded] from this nation.

translation_notes: למען (L-M-ʿ-N): H4616 'on account of / in order that.' Standard purposive conjunction.
דם (D-M): H1818 'blood.' Straightforward.
כל (K-L): Candidates: H3605 'all/whole', H3606 same (Aramaic). Chose H3605.
מיום (M-Y-W-M): Candidates: H3117 'day', H3118 'day (Aramaic)'. Chose H3117 with prefix מ 'from.'
העולם (H-ʿ-W-L-M): H5769 'concealed/time out of mind/eternity/world.' Here 'the world' as in the created order.
עד (ʿ-D): Candidates: H5703 'terminus/duration', H5704 'until/as far as', H5705-5708 various. Chose H5704 — 'until' connecting a time span.
מזאת (M-Z-ʾ-T): Prefix מ 'from' + H2063 זאת 'this (fem.).' 'From this nation.'
textual_notes: מכם could be 'from you (plural)' addressing the audience directly, while מזאת האומה 'from this nation' at the end broadens it. The sentence may be saying the blood will be demanded 'from you' meaning 'from this nation' — the two phrases may be in apposition or the latter may clarify the former.

verses.literal: In order that will be required from you [the] blood [of] all the prophets from [the] day that was created the world until now from this the nation.

verses.translation: From the blood of Hevel [Abel] to the blood of Zechariah, which was poured out between the altar and the house [or: temple]. Yes — and therefore I say to you, it will be required [or: demanded] from this generation.

translation_notes: הבל (H-B-L): Candidates: H1891 'to be vain', H1892 'vanity/emptiness', H1893 'Hebel (Abel), son of Adam', H1077 'not at all', H1078 'Bel', H1079 'heart'. Chose H1893 because 'from the blood of Abel' is a coherent reference to the first murder, and the context traces prophetic bloodshed from the beginning.
עד (ʿ-D): Candidates: H5703-5708. Chose H5704 'until' — marking the range from Abel to Zechariah.
זכריה (Z-K-R-Y-H): H2148 'Zechariah.' A proper name.
במזבח (B-M-Z-B-Ḥ): Candidates: H4196 'altar', H2076-2078 various. Chose H4196 with prefix ב — 'at the altar.'
ובבית (W-B-B-Y-T): Candidates: H1004 'house', H1005/1006 variants. Chose H1004 — 'and in the house/temple.'
כן (K-N): Candidates: H3651 'so/thus/yes', H3652 'so', H3653 'pedestal', H3654 'gnat'. Chose H3651 — 'yes/indeed' as an affirmative before the concluding statement.
ולכן (W-L-K-N): Prefix ו + ל + H3651 כן. 'And therefore.'
אני (ʾ-N-Y): Candidates: H589 'I', H590 'ship/fleet'. Chose H589 — first person pronoun.
אומר: Participle of אמר — 'saying/I say.' The Strong's candidate H201 'Omar (name)' does not fit; this is the active participle of H559.
מזה (M-Z-H): Candidates: H4198 'exhausted', H4199 'Mizzah (name)', H2088 'this', H2089 'sheep', H2090 'this/that'. Chose prefix מ + H2088 זה 'this' = 'from this.'

הדור (H-D-W-R): Candidates: H1752 'to gyrate', H1753 'to reside', H1754 'circle/ball', H1755 'generation/age', H1756 'Dor (place)'. Chose H1755 because 'from this generation' completes the demand for accountability.
textual_notes: כן before ולכן is somewhat unusual. It could be read as an affirmative 'yes' reinforcing what precedes, or it could be a scribal doubling. Another reading: במזבח ובבית כן could mean 'between the altar and the house' with כן acting as a connector, though this is awkward. The phrase likely means 'at the altar and in the house — so it is — and therefore...'

אומר: The only Strong's candidate provided (H201 'Omar') is a proper name. This is clearly the active participle of אמר (H559) meaning 'saying/I say.' The candidate list did not include the verbal form.

verses.literal: From [the] blood [of] Hevel until [the] blood [of] Zechariah that was poured out at the altar and in the house. Yes and therefore I say to you it will be required from this the generation.

verses.translation: Woe [grief, lamentation] to you, wise ones in the law [or: decree, statute], who have taken away the key [or: opener] of wisdom — and you yourselves do not enter, and you prevent [hold back] those who desire this day to enter

translation_notes: אוי: Candidates: H188 'lamentation/Oh!/Woe', H189 'Evi, a Midianite chief'. Chose H188 because this is clearly an exclamatory opening — 'Woe to you' — fitting the denunciatory tone directed at the wise ones.

מפתח: Candidates: H4668 'key/opener', H4669 'aperture/utterance'. Testing H4668 'key of wisdom' — produces a coherent image of someone who holds the instrument of access to wisdom. H4669 'utterance of wisdom' is possible but less vivid given the verb נשא (carried away) and the imagery of entering/not entering that follows. Chose H4668 because the passage builds a metaphor around entry (entering, preventing entry), and a 'key' fits that spatial metaphor perfectly.

בדת: Candidates: H1881 'royal edict/statute', H1882 same meaning (Aramaic form). Both mean law/statute/decree. Chose H1881 because the surrounding text is Hebrew and 'wise in the law' makes perfect contextual sense as a description of legal scholars.
textual_notes: נכנסין and ליכנס use the root כנס which is a late/rabbinic Hebrew form (not attested in classical biblical Hebrew with a Strong's number). The participial ending -ין is Aramaic/Mishnaic in form, suggesting this text is post-biblical or from a dialect mixing biblical and rabbinic Hebrew.
מונעין likewise uses the Aramaic/rabbinic participial suffix -ין rather than biblical -ים, reinforcing the late linguistic register.

שנשאתם could be parsed as ש + נשאתם ('that you carried/took away') from root נשא H5375. The verb נשא can mean 'to lift, carry, take away.' The sense 'you have taken away the key' fits the accusatory context.
אותם could be read as the direct object marker את + them (those whom you prevent), functioning as a relative clause object with שחפצים.

verses.literal: Woe to you wise [ones] in the law who have carried away [the] key of the wisdom and you [are] not entering and you [are] preventing those who desire today to enter

verses.translation: And when he spoke these words to them

translation_notes: וכאשר: The כ prefix + אשר. Candidates for אשר: H833 'to be straight', H834 'who/which/when/where', H835 'happiness', H836 'Asher (person/tribe)', H837 'happiness', H838 'a step'. Chose H834 because כאשר ('as/when') is the standard temporal conjunction, and this clause is clearly introducing a temporal setting: 'and when he said...'

אמר: Candidates: H559 'to say', H560 Aramaic 'to say', H561 'something said', H562 Aramaic 'something said', H563 'a lamb', H564 'Immer (name)'. Chose H559 because this is clearly a verb in context — 'he said these words' — and H559 is the Hebrew verbal form.

אלה: Candidates: H421 'to bewail', H422 'to adjure/imprecate', H423 'imprecation', H424 'oak/strong tree', H425 'Elah (name)', H426 'God'. However, אלה also serves as the Hebrew demonstrative pronoun 'these' (not always listed in Strong's as a separate entry but well-known as a demonstrative). In context — 'these the words' — the demonstrative pronoun is the only coherent reading. None of the listed Strong's candidates fit this syntactic position.
textual_notes: אלה is functioning here as the demonstrative pronoun 'these,' which is not among the Strong's candidates provided. The standard Strong's number for this demonstrative is H428. None of the listed candidates (H421–H426) fit this context. The identification is certain from syntax — it must be the demonstrative pronoun modifying הדברים.

verses.literal: And when he said these the words to them

verses.translation: They were lying in wait [or: ambushing] him, and seeking from his mouth any word [or: matter] by which they could inform against him [or: accuse, slander him]. And [he was] saying to the crowds [or: peoples]: When you see a cloud [or: thundercloud] facing the west, immediately you say 'Rain is coming' — and the rain comes.

translation_notes: אי (consonants אי): Candidates: H335 'where/how', H336 'not', H337 'alas', H338 'wild creature', H339 'coast/island'. Chose H335 because אי זה דבר = 'what thing / which matter' — forming an interrogative phrase about what word they might catch.

דבר (consonants דבר): Candidates: H1696 'to speak', H1697 'a word/matter/thing', H1698 'pestilence', H1699 'pasture'. Chose H1697 because 'some thing/word' from his mouth that could be used to accuse him is the natural reading.

ענן (consonants ענן): Candidates: H6049 'to practice magic', H6050 'cloud (Aramaic)', H6051 'cloud/thundercloud', H6052 'Anan (name)'. Chose H6051 because 'you see a cloud facing the west' is a weather observation.
נגד (consonants נגד): H5048 'opposite/facing' — a cloud facing/approaching from the west.
מערב (consonants מערב): Candidates: H4627 'traffic/goods', H4628 'the west'. Chose H4628 because a cloud approaching from the west bringing rain is a well-known weather pattern in the land of Israel.
מיד (consonants מ+יד): H3027 'hand' — מיד literally 'from hand' idiomatically means 'immediately/at once'.
המטר: Candidates: H4305 'to rain (verb)', H4306 'rain (noun)'. Chose H4306 (noun) because both instances use the article ה, indicating 'the rain' as a noun.
textual_notes: The brackets ] [ in the text appear to mark a textual break or lacuna between the accusation scene and the weather teaching. The two segments may originally have been separate passages.
להלשינו is a post-biblical Hebrew hiphil infinitive from the root לשן (tongue), meaning 'to inform against, to slander, to accuse' — no Strong's entry provided.
לעמים could be 'to the peoples' (עם, H5971) or 'to the crowds'. In post-biblical Hebrew עמים can function as 'crowds/masses'.

verses.literal: Lying in ambush [for] him and seeking from his mouth some thing [by which] they could accuse him. And [he was] saying to the peoples: When you see [a] cloud opposite [the] west, immediately you say rain will come, and the rain comes.
